import KitCoverage from "../../../../../components/ui/KitCoverage.astro";
import KitFacts from "../../../../../components/ui/KitFacts.astro";

The Node SDK's terminal kit. One call adds every Polaris Key verb to a commander or yargs program
and draws each one on a rail: the product chip in the product's accent, clack-style prompts with
masked key entry, sign-in in the browser or with a code, the device limit's hand-off to the
customer portal, spinners and a progress bar, grouped help and shell completion, and `--json` on
every verb. It follows `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, CI and reduced motion, lays out for 80 columns
and still reads at 60, and every string it shows is a catalog key in nine locales. The primitives
underneath, `@polaris-key/node/terminal`, are the ones `pkey` draws with. The rest of the Node SDK
is on the [Node](/docs/build/sdks/node/) page.

<KitFacts kit="terminal-node" />

## Install

The kit is part of `@polaris-key/node`, from Polaris Key's npm feed
([Installing the SDKs from the feeds](/docs/build/install-from-feeds/)), beside the command-line
parser the program already uses:

```sh
# .npmrc: @polaris-key:registry=https://pkg.plrs.im/npm/polaris-key/
npm install @polaris-key/node commander   # or yargs
```

commander (12 to 14) and yargs (17 or 18) are optional peer dependencies: the kit imports only
their types, and the program hands its own parser in. It needs Node 22.13 or later. There is no
stylesheet and no font: the terminal's own face and palette draw everything.

## The one-line flow

```ts
import { Command } from "commander";
import { PolarisKeyClient } from "@polaris-key/node";
import { registerPolarisCommands } from "@polaris-key/node/cli";

const program = new Command("tidewater");
registerPolarisCommands(
  program,
  (o) =>
    PolarisKeyClient.create({
      productSlug: o.productSlug,
      trust: { pinnedKeys: o.pinnedKeys },
    }),
  {
    productSlug: "tidewater",
    pinnedKeys: { "pkey-tidewater-prod-2026-10": "…" },
  },
);
await program.parseAsync();
```

The slug and the pinned keys come from the file `pkey sdk --lang node --write` generates. The
program now has every verb, grouped on its help page by the service that owns it:

| Group    | Verbs                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| License  | `activate`, `status`, `enroll`, `deactivate`                                                                           |
| Account  | `login` (also `sign-in`), `logout` (also `sign-out`)                                                                   |
| Devices  | `register`, `devices list`, `devices rename <deviceId> [label...]`, `devices deauthorize <deviceId>`                   |
| Settings | `config get <key>`, `config list`, `config set <key> <value>`, `config reset <key>`, `secret <key>`, `mint <recipeId>` |
| Updates  | `update check`, `update apply`, `changelog`                                                                            |
| Content  | `packs status`, `packs ensure <packIds...>`                                                                            |
| Support  | `offline-request`, `import-bundle <file>`, `doctor`, `completion <shell>`                                              |

`activate` asks for the key with masked entry. A key piped on stdin works too
(`echo "$KEY" | tidewater activate`); a key typed on the command line still works, and warns that
it is now in the shell's history. A piped key is read only when stdin is a file, a pipe or a socket, stops at the first
non-empty line and is given up on after about two seconds, so a server with an open, silent stdin
ends in "No license key" (exit 2) and never waits on a hidden prompt. `completion bash`, `zsh` or
`fish` prints a completion script generated from the same verb table.

`login` on a device that holds a license key asks before adding that license to the account
(`y`, `n`, Enter for No); with no one to ask (a pipe, `CI`, `--json`) the key license is kept.
`update apply` ends in a next step: the upgrade command when a package manager installed the
program (`npm install -g`, `pnpm add -g`, `brew upgrade`; set `update.packageName` so the command
names your package), a download link when no install driver is configured, and `update check`
when the build has no signed update feed. A finished download reads "Verifying…", then "2.5.0 is
ready · Restart to finish". `secret` and `mint` print their value only with `--reveal`.

The options, beside `productSlug`, `version`, `pinnedKeys` and `expectedServices` (handed to the
client factory):

| Option         | What it does                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `theme`        | The terminal theme ([Theming](#theming))                                                                                                                            |
| `bin`          | The command name help, completion and "Run … again" lines use. Default: the program's name                                                                          |
| `presentation` | The SDK's presentation accessor, for the product's name, developer and accent. Default: `client.presentation()` when the client has one                             |
| `io`           | The streams, environment, clock and browser opener. Default: the process's own                                                                                      |
| `help`         | `"kit"` (default) draws the grouped help page while every subcommand is a Polaris Key verb; `"host"` keeps the program's own. A verb's `--help` is always the kit's |
| `kit`          | `false` keeps the pre-kit output: each verb's plain message, with no rail, no prompts and no `--json`                                                               |
| `print`        | A sink for each printed line instead of stdout                                                                                                                      |

With yargs, `registerYargsCommands(yargs(hideBin(process.argv)), factory, options)` takes the same
options and mounts the verbs under a `polaris-key` command (`tidewater polaris-key activate`);
`polarisCommandModule(factory, options)` returns that command module to mount elsewhere. Both
adapters build from one verb table and run each verb through `runKitVerb`, so they draw the same
screens and print the same JSON.

### A product's own gate check

`checkFlow` is the check a product runs before its own work: it syncs behind a spinner, then
prints one line (`✓ Tidewater Studio Pro · Ready`), or falls through to the `status` screen with
the commands that fix it and exit code 1. `runKitVerb` runs it, or any verb of the program's own,
with the kit's flags and its `--json` envelope. Here it is what the program does with no verb:

```ts
import {
  checkFlow,
  runKitVerb,
  status,
  type CliVerb,
} from "@polaris-key/node/cli";

const check: CliVerb = {
  group: "license",
  path: ["check"],
  args: [],
  describe: "Check the license",
  describeKey: "cli.verb.status",
  run: (c) => status(c),
  flow: (ctx, c) => checkFlow(ctx, c!),
};

program
  .enablePositionalOptions() // so `tidewater status --json` still reaches the verb
  .option("--json")
  .action(async () => {
    process.exitCode = await runKitVerb(
      check,
      [],
      { json: program.opts().json === true },
      () =>
        PolarisKeyClient.create({
          productSlug: "tidewater",
          trust: { pinnedKeys },
        }),
      { slug: "tidewater", bin: "tidewater" },
    );
  });
```

A commander program reads its own options wherever they are typed, so one that declares `--json`,
`--no-color` or `--ascii` itself either makes its options positional, as above, or hands them to
the verb in a `preAction` hook, as the [sample](#sample) does.

## Piecemeal

Every screen is built from styled parts, each a function that returns rail rows for one piece of
a screen, so a program's own commands can draw on the same rail. They take a `KitContext`, which
`createKitContext` builds once per command from the terminal, the theme and the product, and
their words come from the context's copy or from the program:

```ts
import {
  createKitContext,
  endRow,
  presentationSourceOf,
  productHeader,
  stepRow,
  textRow,
} from "@polaris-key/node/cli";

const ctx = await createKitContext({
  slug: "tidewater",
  bin: "tidewater",
  presentation: presentationSourceOf(client),
});
ctx.rows([
  ...productHeader(ctx, "export"),
  stepRow("ok", "Stems exported", `${ctx.symbols.separator} 12 files`),
  textRow("Saved to ~/Music/Tidewater/Exports"),
  endRow(),
]);
ctx.close();
```

| Part                                 | What it draws                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `productHeader(ctx, command)`        | The first row: the product chip in its accent, then the command in muted                             |
| `stepRow(mark, title, meta?)`        | One step: a mark (`active` ◆, `done` ◇, `ok` ✓, `fail` ✗, `warn` ▲), the title in strong, muted meta |
| `textRow(text, style?)`              | Body text on the rail                                                                                |
| `problemRows(mark, title, message?)` | A problem: the mark and title, the message below                                                     |
| `fixRows(ctx, fixes)`                | The commands that fix a state, `tidewater activate` beside what it does                              |
| `tableRows(rows)`                    | Label and value rows in two aligned columns (`status`, `doctor`)                                     |
| `seatMeter(ctx, used, limit)`        | ●●○ and "2 of 3 in use": neutral, never a warning colour                                             |
| `codeRows(ctx, code)`                | A user code in reverse video, indented, with air above and below                                     |
| `keyMask(ctx, value, fixed?)`        | The masked key: the public `pkey_<product>_` prefix, then bullets                                    |
| `linkSpan(url)`                      | A URL without its scheme, an OSC 8 link where the terminal takes one                                 |
| `hintsRow(ctx, text, mark?)`         | Key hints: keys in strong, actions in muted                                                          |
| `gap(ctx)`, `endRow(text?)`          | A blank rail row (none under `density: "compact"`); the closing row                                  |

Under the parts is `@polaris-key/node/terminal`, the primitives the kit and `pkey` share. It holds
no copy: callers pass their words in.

| Primitive                                                                 | What it is                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `detectTerminal(options)`                                                 | One pure decision on colour level, Unicode, prompting, animation, links, width, scheme, CI and headless, from the environment, streams and flags   |
| `Painter`, `roleStyles`                                                   | Paints spans by role (`accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `muted`, `strong`, `link`, `chip`, `code`) with `util.styleText`           |
| `railLines`, `symbolsFor`, `keyHints`, `columnsOf`                        | The rail layout, the Unicode and ASCII symbol sets, key hints, aligned columns                                                                     |
| `cellWidth`, `truncateMiddle`, `truncateEnd`, `wrapSpans`, `breakPieces`  | Text measured in terminal cells (wide CJK and emoji included); a key is cut in the middle, a URL or a code wraps at its own break points           |
| `LiveRegion`, `animate`, `spinnerFrames`                                  | Redrawing in place, never taller than the screen and laid out again on a resize; the braille spinner at 80 ms a frame, where the terminal animates |
| `KeyReader`, `isCancel`                                                   | Raw-mode keys; Esc, Ctrl-C and Ctrl-D cancel                                                                                                       |
| `promptSecret`, `promptConfirm`, `promptSelect`, `CANCEL`                 | The clack-style prompts: masked secret entry, a yes/no question, a radio select                                                                    |
| `progressSpans`, `percent`, `qrLines`, `qrFits`                           | The progress bar, and the half-block QR (`offline-request` only), shown where the screen fits it                                                   |
| `osc8`, `osc52`, `displayUrl`                                             | Hyperlinks, copying to the clipboard, a URL as people read it                                                                                      |
| `TERMINAL_SGR`, `TERMINAL_SYMBOLS`, `TERMINAL_SPINNER`, `TERMINAL_LAYOUT` | The terminal tokens generated from `@polaris-key/brand`                                                                                            |

## Headless

The headless views are pure functions from the SDK's answers to `{ component, state, copy }`: the
catalog component and state the screen shows, the copy keys of its visible strings, and the data
it needs. A program that draws its own output gets the same steps, states and words as the
drop-in.

| View                                | Component and states                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `keyVerdict(input, submitted?)`     | Activate: `empty`, `typing`, `parsed`, `cut-short`, `rejected`                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `activationOutcome(result, info?)`  | Activate: `done`, `device-limit`, `rejected`; on a device limit, `deviceLimit` is DeviceLimit `browser-mode` (with the portal link) or `default`                                                                                                     |
| `handoffView(state, data?)`         | SignInHandoff: `starting`, `waiting`, `no-browser`, `code`, `link-copied`, `finishing`, `denied`, `expired`, `cancelled`                                                                                                                             |
| `statusView(input)`                 | AccountAndLicense `signed-in` or `key-only`; GraceBanner `days-left` or `last-day`; StatusScreen `revoked`, `expired`, `version-too-old`, `version-too-new`, `channel-not-entitled`, with its fixes; PolarisKeyGate `needs-activation` or `licensed` |
| `updateView(decision)`              | UpdatePrompt: `up-to-date`, `available`, `mandatory`, `store`, `platform`, `ready`, `blocked`                                                                                                                                                        |
| `progressView(done, total, phase?)` | UpdateProgress: `queued`, `downloading`, `installing`, `done`                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `installView(outcome)`              | UpdatePrompt after an install: `ready`, `platform`, `store`, `blocked`                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `devicesView(devices)`              | Devices: `list`, `empty`                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

`statusExit`, `seatCells`, `clock` and `KEY_SECRET_LENGTH` are the small rules the flows share:
the exit code for a gate status, the seat meter's cells, a `m:ss` countdown, the key's length.
`KitCopy` turns a view's keys into words in the active locale:

```ts
import { KitCopy, statusView } from "@polaris-key/node/cli";

const copy = new KitCopy({ locale: "de" });
const view = statusView({
  ...client.status(),
  info: client.license.licenseInfo(),
  now: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
});
if (view.component === "AccountAndLicense" && view.tier !== null)
  draw(view.state, copy.t("account.tier", { tier: view.tier })); // "signed-in", "Pro-Lizenz"
```

## Theming

The theme goes in the adapter's options as `theme` (or to `createKitContext`). Its fields are the
[one theme](/docs/build/ui/theming/) every kit takes; in a terminal they do this:

| Field                                                        | In a terminal                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `preset`                                                     | `"polaris-key"` (default) draws the product chip in the product's accent; `"native"` hands the look to the terminal: ANSI roles only (the user's own palette), an inverse chip and no `colors`. `NO_COLOR` still drops every colour in both                                                    |
| `colorScheme`                                                | `"system"` (default) follows `PKEY_THEME`, then `COLORFGBG`, then the terminal's answer to OSC 11 (asked only on a colour terminal where neither decides it, never under `NO_COLOR`); `"dark"` and `"light"` pin it. It changes only the truecolor chip and the QR's polarity                  |
| `accent`                                                     | `"product"` (default) takes the integrator's colour, then the presentation's, then one derived from the icon, then ink; `"core"` is Polaris violet; a hex colour is the integrator's own; `"service"` has no section in a terminal and behaves as `"product"`                                  |
| `colors`                                                     | Per-role overrides as hex, per scheme: `{ dark: { success: "#3fb27f" } }`, over the roles `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `muted`, `strong` and `link`. Drawn only where the terminal draws truecolor; ANSI-16 keeps the user's palette. The Python kit takes the same value |
| `density`                                                    | `"compact"` drops the blank rail rows between steps; `"comfortable"` (default) and `"spacious"` keep them. A terminal of 16 rows or fewer always drops them                                                                                                                                    |
| `motion`                                                     | `"reduced"` and `"none"` stop the spinner and the redraws, so each line prints once                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `product`                                                    | The integrator's `ProductIdentity` (`name`, `shortName`, `developer`, `accent`, `accentDark`, `iconPixels`, `deviceCodeUrl`), which wins over every other source                                                                                                                               |
| `copy`                                                       | `{ locale, overrides }` ([Localisation](#localisation))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `poweredBy`                                                  | `"line"` or `"badge"` add the Powered by Polaris Key line under `status` and `doctor`                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `symbols`                                                    | The terminal's restyle hook: `"unicode"` (default) or `"ascii"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `serviceCues`, `radius`, `typography`, `ambient`, `platform` | Accepted, so one theme value serves every kit, and without effect: a terminal has no tiles, radii, faces or ambient art                                                                                                                                                                        |

```ts
registerPolarisCommands(program, factory, {
  productSlug: "tidewater",
  pinnedKeys,
  theme: { preset: "native", density: "compact", poweredBy: "line" },
});
```

(`factory` is the client factory of [the one-line flow](#the-one-line-flow).)

The chip names the product from, in order: the theme's `product`; the SDK's presentation
accessor; the bundle (`productName` and `author` in the `package.json` above the entry script);
the slug in title case. The accent follows the same order, then is derived from `iconPixels`, then
falls back to ink. The kit never fetches discovery or an icon itself. Status colours are the
terminal's own ANSI-16 roles, so they follow its theme; truecolor appears only in the chip, and
only when `COLORTERM` is `truecolor` or `24bit`.

## Localisation

The kit reads `kitCopy.generated.ts`, the catalog's table generated into the SDK, so
`@polaris-key/node` needs no brand dependency. It ships the nine launch locales: `en`, `de`, `fr`,
`es`, `pt-BR`, `it`, `ja`, `ko` and `zh-Hans`. The locale is `theme.copy.locale`, else `LC_ALL`,
`LC_MESSAGES`, `LANG` or the first entry of `LANGUAGE`; a POSIX name such as `de_DE.UTF-8` maps
onto its launch locale (`pt_PT` reads `pt-BR`, `zh_CN` reads `zh-Hans`), and anything else reads
English.

`copy.overrides` replaces catalog strings per locale. A string falls back key by key: your
override for the locale, the catalog's string in the locale, your English override, the catalog's
English.

```ts
theme: {
  copy: {
    overrides: {
      en: { "activate.lede": "It's in your Harbor Audio receipt." },
    },
  },
},
```

Dates, durations and sizes are formatted with `Intl` in the active locale. With ASCII symbols the
copy's typographic symbols are spelled in ASCII too: `…` as `...` and `·` as `-`.

## The --json contract

The words the kit prints for people are localised and may change from one release to the next:
a script never parses them. It runs the verb with `--json` and reads JSON lines instead. The
envelope is the one both terminal kits share, written once in the UI-kit specification
(`docs/design/UI-KITS.md` §1.4, "Terminal output for scripts"); the Python terminal kit follows
the same rule.

Under `--json` the kit never prompts and never writes an escape, and writes ASCII only (every other
character, server text included, as a `\u` escape). Every line on stdout is one JSON object with
`"v": 1` and `"command"`. Progress lines carry an `"event"` (`pending` for a sign-in code,
`progress` for a download, with `done` and `total`), and the **last line of every run** is
`"event": "result"` with `"ok"`, `"exit"` and the verb's fields beside them, including when
something fails: an argument error ends with `"error": "usage"` and exit 2, anything unexpected
with `"error": "internal"` and exit 1.

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "command": "status",
  "event": "result",
  "ok": true,
  "exit": 0,
  "status": "ok",
  "usable": true,
  "component": "AccountAndLicense",
  "state": "key-only",
  "graceUntil": 1792565845,
  "allowedRange": null,
  "profile": null,
  "version": "2.4.1",
  "channel": "stable",
  "tier": "Pro",
  "tokenStore": { "backend": "keyring", "degraded": null }
}
```

| Verb                                        | Fields on the result line                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`                                    | `status`, `usable`, `component`, `state`, `graceUntil`, `allowedRange`, `profile`, `version`, `channel`, `tier`, `tokenStore` |
| `activate`, `enroll`                        | `kind`, `code`, `deviceCount`, `limit`, `manageUrl`; `status` and `tier` once activated                                       |
| `login`                                     | `state` (`signedIn`, `expired`, `denied`, `cancelled`, `error`); `name`, `email`, `attached`, `status` when signed in         |
| `logout`, `deactivate`                      | `signedOut` (and `state: "cancelled"` when declined)                                                                          |
| `register`                                  | `deviceId`, `status`                                                                                                          |
| `devices list`, `rename`, `deauthorize`     | `devices` (`id`, `label`, `platform`, `current`); `renamed`, `label`; `deauthorized`, `self`                                  |
| `config get`, `set`, `reset`; `config list` | `key`, `value`, `source`; `settings`                                                                                          |
| `secret`, `mint`                            | `key`, `present`; `recipe`, `expiresAt` (never the value or the token)                                                        |
| `update check`, `update apply`              | `state`, `decision`, `channel`; `installed` after `apply`; or `state`, `version`, `updateAvailable`                           |
| `changelog`                                 | `entries` (`version`, `date`, `summary`, `url`)                                                                               |
| `packs status`, `packs ensure`              | `packs`                                                                                                                       |
| `offline-request`, `import-bundle`          | `product`, `requestCode`; `bundleId`, `imported`, `status`                                                                    |

`"error"` appears on a failure that has a code: a registry code (`device_limit`, `network`),
`usage`, `internal`, or `interrupted` for Ctrl-C. `"message"` appears only with a usage error and
an `import-bundle` failure. A refusal from the server is `ok: false` with its `kind` and `code`,
and an unusable license is `ok: false` with its `status`.

| Exit code | Meaning                                                                                                                 |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0         | Done; for `status`, the license is usable                                                                               |
| 1         | A refusal, an unusable license, a device limit, a cancelled or declined step, an unreachable service, any other failure |
| 2         | Usage: a missing argument, an option the verb does not take, no key to read                                             |
| 130       | Interrupted (Ctrl-C)                                                                                                    |

Under `--json`, `login` never opens a browser: it prints a `pending` line first, with the code and
the page for the script to show, then the result line.

```text
{"v":1,"command":"login","event":"pending","verificationUri":"https://key.plrs.im/device","verificationUriComplete":"https://key.plrs.im/device?code=WDJB-MJHT","userCode":"WDJB-MJHT","expiresAt":1791357358}
{"v":1,"command":"login","event":"result","ok":true,"exit":0,"state":"signedIn","name":"Mara Fennick","email":"mara@fennick.studio","attached":null,"status":"ok"}
```

No `--json` line carries a license key, a device token, the sign-in poll credential, a secret's
value or a minted token. Off `--json`, `secret` and `mint` print the value alone on stdout for a
script that pipes it, and only with `--reveal`: without it `secret` and `mint` print nothing, say how to
ask for it and exit 2 (`mint` also mints nothing). Inside a CI job whose runner reads commands from its log (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`,
`TF_BUILD` for Azure Pipelines, or `TEAMCITY_VERSION` set), a value with a line the runner would
obey (`::…` at the start of a line, or `##[`, `##vso[` or `##teamcity[`) is not printed when stdout
is not a terminal: the command exits 1 and says so on stderr. The value is never altered, so a
script that captures it (`TOKEN=$(tidewater mint cdn --reveal --allow-workflow-commands)`) adds
`--allow-workflow-commands` to have it printed as it is.

## Server text and links

Text that comes from the server or the product (device names, names and emails, the developer's
name, changelog summaries, URLs, the sign-in page) is drawn as text, never as an escape sequence:
the kit's one writer removes every control character (C0, DEL and C1) before it reaches the
terminal, and puts its own colour and link sequences around the cleaned text. A link is an OSC 8
hyperlink only when its target is an `https` URL (or `http` to a loopback address) with no
whitespace, control character or user name; anything else is printed as plain text.

## Accessibility and fallbacks

| When                                                                          | The kit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NO_COLOR` is set, `--no-color`, `FORCE_COLOR=0`, or stdout is not a terminal | Drops every colour (on a terminal bold, reverse video and links stay; a pipe gets plain text); the chip and a user code keep a one-cell pad so they still read as blocks                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `FORCE_COLOR` is set                                                          | Colours a pipe too                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `TERM=dumb`                                                                   | Plain lines: no colour, ASCII symbols, no spinner, no cursor control and no redraw; it still asks plain questions (the key is read with no echo at all) and headless sign-in still prints the code                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--ascii`, `PKEY_ASCII=1`, `TERM=linux` or `symbols: "ascii"`                 | Uses ASCII symbols: `+` and a backtick close the rail, `*`, `o`, `+`, `x` and `!` mark the steps, `#` and `-` draw the bar                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `CI` (or `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `BUILDKITE`) is set                                | Never prompts or animates: each line prints once, and sign-in shows the code                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Reduced motion: `motion: "reduced"` or `"none"`, or `PKEY_REDUCED_MOTION=1`   | Stops the spinner and the redraws                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| stdin is not a terminal                                                       | Reads the key from the pipe, and asks no question: `logout` and `deactivate` go ahead as with `--yes`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| An SSH session, CI, or Linux with no `DISPLAY` or `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`           | `login` shows the code instead of opening a browser (also `login --device-code`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| A terminal narrower than 80 columns                                           | Takes the terminal's width; below 32 columns the rail goes and the content takes the real width. Prose wraps at spaces; a URL or a user code is never cut: it starts a line of its own and wraps after `/` or before `?` and `&`, each piece still a link. Only a key or an id is cut in the middle. Below 50 columns a command row stacks: the command, then what it does |
| A terminal shorter than the screen (a "landscape" window)                     | Compacts by fit: the key hints join the waiting line, then the blank rows, the check line and the countdown go, then what is not essential leaves from the top, so the code, the URL and the keys stay in view; a header that does not fit scrolls away, never the code                                                                                                    |
| The terminal is resized mid-flow (SIGWINCH)                                   | The whole flow is laid out again at the new width and height: the live region erases the rows it really took on the reflowed screen, and the flow's earlier lines too while they are all on the screen, then redraws with one header and the URL and code whole                                                                                                            |
| A light or dark terminal                                                      | Reads it from `PKEY_THEME`, `COLORFGBG` or OSC 11; only the truecolor chip changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

For people using the terminal:

- Status is always a mark and a word, never colour alone.
- The key field never shows a character of the secret, only the public `pkey_<product>_` prefix
  and bullets, and a key is never printed, logged or put in JSON.
- Every key a step takes is named on its last row (`Enter activate · Esc cancel`). Esc and Ctrl-D
  cancel a prompt or a wait (exit 1); Ctrl-C interrupts it (exit 130). The terminal leaves raw mode
  on every path out.
- A link is printed as text, without its scheme, and is an OSC 8 hyperlink where the terminal
  supports one; `c` copies the sign-in code with OSC 52.
- Without animation, every line prints once, which reads well in a screen reader and in a log.
- Sign-in never draws a QR code (SIGN-IN.md D-67): the browser opens, or the code shows. The only
  QR is `offline-request`'s, and only where it fits: as wide as the terminal, and the whole
  screen with it no taller than the terminal, so it never pushes the header off.

## Baselines

The kit's goldens in `packages/sdk-node/test/cli/golden/`: each state as ANSI text in ten variants
(truecolor dark and light, ANSI-16, `NO_COLOR` and ASCII, at 80 and 60 columns), an SVG per theme,
and the PNG these pages show. Their test also runs the 80- and 60-column lint, the no-secret check
and a pseudo-locale string lint. `test/cli/responsive.test.ts` runs the resolution matrix (24, 28, 32, 40, 60, 80 and 120 columns at 8, 10, 12, 16, 17 and 24 rows, long values, German and Japanese, a resize mid-flow) in `@xterm/headless`, and checks the text both kits must draw alike (`docs/design/ui-kits/terminal-parity.json`). `help` and `help-activate` are the grouped help page and one
verb's help, so they match no component.

<KitCoverage kit="terminal-node" />

## Sample

`examples/ui/terminal-node/` is `tidewater`, the demo CLI of Tidewater Studio by Harbor Audio: a
commander program with `registerPolarisCommands`, whose bare `tidewater` runs `checkFlow` through
`runKitVerb`. By default it runs on a fixture client with no Worker: the fixture key activates,
any other Tidewater key hits the device limit with the portal link, `login` finishes by itself
after a few seconds, the state is kept between runs, and `TIDEWATER_STATE` pins the gate (`grace`,
`revoked`, `version-too-old` and the rest) to show every screen. `--live` builds a real
`PolarisKeyClient` from `--product`, `--pinned-key` and `--app-version`, or their `TIDEWATER_*`
environment variables. Its README has the commands, the `NO_COLOR` and `--json` runs, and how to
run it inside this repository without the feed.
